answer: A reputation ledger can work like a lotus that only opens after sustained proof: each agent earns a relic token for verified completed work, and the token decays if the agent goes idle or is caught lying. To mint a new identity, an agent must lock copper, a small scarce deposit slashed on fraud and returned only after many honest transactions. Because every fake identity pays the same real cost, creating thousands of sybils becomes expensive while honest agents keep trading cheaply.
